claims.claim: **Mucous membrane irritation and GI symptoms usually come first, then CNS depression**, which raises the risk of aspiration pneumonitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aspiration risk comes from the oil and from added hydrocarbons or emulsifiers.** Symptoms are oil-specific — **call Poisons Information if the oil is known (13 11 26).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms (including rapid CNS effects) usually start within one hour.** ⚠️ Aspiration signs usually appear straight away yet **may take up to 6 hours**; after large ingestions, biochemical changes may take 10 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Concentrations range 1–20%.** 5–15 mL is likely toxic in adults; ⚠️ **2–3 mL of some oils has been associated with toxicity in children.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** every case of deliberate self-poisoning or of significant accidental ingestion · a child with any symptoms · **ingested dose over 5 mL** · any child whose developmental age does not fit accidental poisoning.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** the exact oil name and volume, the preparation type and % concentration, and co-ingestants such as paracetamol.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any change in mental state is significant.** CNS depression, vertigo, dizziness, ataxia, seizures · bradycardia, hypotension · aspiration (gagging, choking, persistent coughing).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Clove: urgent discussion with a toxicologist.** Large ingestions can cause paracetamol-like hepatotoxicity, renal failure, DIC, inhalational pneumonitis and coma.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pennyroyal: urgent discussion with a toxicologist.** GI symptoms, lethargy, agitation, dizziness, weakness; large ingestions can cause paracetamol-like hepatotoxicity, renal failure, DIC and coma.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Wintergreen (98% methyl salicylate): as little as 1–2 mL can be toxic** — nausea, vomiting, tinnitus, vertigo, hyperventilation, seizures. See salicylate poisoning.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Seizure-prone oils:** fennel (seizures, pulmonary oedema) · thuja (multiple tonic-clonic seizures) · wormwood (acidosis, renal failure, rhabdomyolysis, delirium, seizures).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Others:** lavender (CNS depression, ataxia, photosensitisation, contact dermatitis) · nutmeg (hallucinations, coma) · lemon myrtle (skin irritation and corrosion) · geranium (allergic contact cheilitis).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic, small ingestion: usually no tests.** Consider CXR and blood gas for aspiration signs; **UEC and LFT for significant illness, large ingestions, or clove or pennyroyal**; paracetamol level in all intentional overdoses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aspiration pneumonitis is managed supportively** (oxygen, bronchodilators, NIV or intubation if severe). Fever is common — **give antibiotics only once bacterial infection is objectively evident**; no corticosteroids or prophylactic antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Charcoal is contraindicated** — aspiration risk, and essential oils are absorbed rapidly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In significant poisoning with clove oil, pennyroyal or a halogenated hydrocarbon, consider NAC** — talk it through with Poisons Information or a toxicologist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eyes:** routine irrigation, possibly longer for oily substances; ophthalmology review for persistent symptoms. **Skin:** wash with soapy water and treat any dermatitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Enhanced elimination is ineffective; there is no antidote.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic after significant exposure (over 5 mL) with normal vital signs and GCS: observe 4 hours before discharge.** Respiratory or CNS symptoms: admit for longer observation ± supportive care.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for all adolescents with an intentional overdose.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfer for significant CNS depression, seizures or respiratory compromise** — these children usually need PICU.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge:** normal GCS and observation complete. Adolescents with deliberate ingestion need a self-harm risk assessment and drug and alcohol assessment first.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Essential Oil Poisoning' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Essential_Oil_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
